Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing questions will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q3 results. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Innovation Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover our geographic performance in developed versus emerging markets, our key strategic priorities and progress, competitive activity and our responses, organic sales growth guidance for next quarter and the full year, promotional strategy and its effectiveness, capital expenditure plans and priorities, price elasticity observations, and new product launches along with our innovation pipeline update.

I will now turn the call over to John Ramirez to provide more detail on our financial results.

John Ramirez:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $6.4 billion, representing a 5% increase year-over-year, or 5% organic growth on a constant currency basis, exceeding our guidance midpoint. Gross margin expanded 180 basis points to 48.1%, driven by favorable pricing realization, supply chain productivity gains, and a shift toward premium mixes. Adjusted operating income rose 11% to $1.2 billion, with margins expanding 220 basis points to 22.4%. Diluted earnings per share came in at $1.25, up 12% from the prior year. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me dive deeper into our geographic performance, breaking it out between developed and emerging markets—a critical lens for understanding this quarter's results. Developed markets represent about 62% of our quarterly revenue, while emerging markets account for the remaining 38%. This mix has held steady year-over-year, but growth dynamics differ sharply, reflecting macroeconomic tailwinds and our execution with household essentials like our flagship laundry detergent PowerClean, beauty brand GlowEssence, and snack portfolio including CrunchBar.

In developed markets, we achieved resilient organic growth of 3.2%—our strongest quarter in the past year despite ongoing inflation and shifting consumer behaviors. North America, driving 40% of group sales, led with +4.1%, powered by volume gains in fabric care and a 150-basis-point market share expansion per IRI data in the US mass channel. Premiumization was key; PowerClean Ultra, our enzyme-boosted variant, grew 12% in velocity, gaining share from private labels as households traded up amid 7% category inflation. Western Europe grew more modestly at +1.8%, impacted by soft volumes in the UK and Germany from cost-of-living pressures favoring discounters like Aldi and Lidl. However, e-commerce penetration reached 22% of sales, up from 18% last year, via targeted Amazon promotions and our DTC site, which benefited from a 25% uplift in personalized subscriptions.

Margins in developed markets expanded 80 basis points to 28.5%, thanks to supply chain efficiencies from our $150 million North American manufacturing optimization. We're using AI-driven demand forecasting—much like Unilever's Palantir partnership—to cut inventory 15% while keeping 98% on-shelf availability. Sustainability efforts, such as recyclable packaging for GlowEssence shampoos, boosted loyalty scores by 10 points per Nielsen surveys in Europe.

Emerging markets were the standout, growing 8.7% organically and contributing 60% of total volume growth, outpacing our 7-9% long-term target. This highlights our 'aspirational everyday' portfolio in high-potential areas. Asia-Pacific led at +11.2%, with China at +14.5%—our largest emerging market at 12% of group sales. Urban millennials in Tier 2 cities like Chengdu drove GlowEssence via Tmall and JD.com, gaining 2.2 share points amid a 20% beauty category surge post-reopening. India followed at +10.8%, with CrunchBar capitalizing on snacking trends; our Project Shakti rural network of 150,000 micro-entrepreneurs, similar to Hindustan Unilever's model, reached 85% of villages, delivering 18% volume growth despite monsoons.

Latin America grew +7.9%, resilient in Brazil at +9.2% with PowerClean sachets for low-income homes, though Argentina's hyperinflation limited constant currency growth to +5%. Africa grew +6.4%, with Nigeria's out-of-home snack recovery offsetting forex volatility. Margins compressed 50 basis points to 22.1% from raw material costs like cocoa and palm oil up 25% YoY, but localized sourcing—including 40% RSPO-certified palm from Indonesia—helped mitigate FX impacts.

Comparing the two, developed markets provide stability with low-single-digit growth, high-single-digit EBITDA margins, and reliable cash flows supporting our 2.5% dividend yield. Emerging markets offer upside from urbanization and a middle class projected to add 1.5 billion consumers by 2030 per McKinsey, though with volatility from currencies—a 3% FX headwind this quarter—and local rivals like P&G's Ariel in India or Reckitt's Dettol in Southeast Asia. Emerging outgrew developed by 5.5 points, narrowing our sales mix gap from 65/35 two years ago.

Strategically, we're advancing on three fronts: route-to-market innovation like quick-commerce pilots with Indonesia's Gojek for same-day PowerClean delivery, aiming for 15% EM e-commerce mix by FY25; portfolio sharpening, including divesting a low-growth Eastern European hygiene brand for $200 million to fund high-ROIC EM innovations like low-water laundry pods for India; and sustainability as a multiplier—our Planet Positive pledge targets 50% recycled content in EM packs by year-end, unlocking premium pricing akin to Nestlé's emerging hydration efforts.

Now, turning to competitive activity and our responses, which is a dynamic challenge but one we're addressing through targeted actions and strong brand equity. Drawing on IRI and Nielsen data through Q3, let's review by category and region.

In North America, 55% of net sales, intensity rose in household and personal care. P&G's Tide Pods Eco-Refill push gained 1.2 points of ACV in mass, lifting their share to 32%. We held QuickClean detergent at 18.5% share via a preemptive 15% Q2 price increase ahead of the 8% category average, preserving 22% gross margins despite 12% surfactant inflation.

Our multifaceted response included accelerating CleanFuture recyclable pouches to 65% conversion in top IRI outlets, driving 4-point velocity in Costco and Sam's Club. We added $25 million in trade spend, up 20% QoQ, on high-velocity SKUs, reclaiming 150 basis points from private labels like Great Value, now at 14%. Q4 early data shows category NPS at +12 versus competitors' +8.

In snacks and beverages, PepsiCo's Gatorade zero-sugar took 2.1 share points to 42%, and Mondelez's Oreo Thins grew 18%, pressuring VitalEats cookies with a 1% volume dip, especially Midwest.

We relaunched VitalBoost high-protein snacks with plant-based pea protein, backed by $40 million A&P on TikTok and endcaps, gaining 7% distribution in 7-Eleven and Circle K, with velocity 9 points above average. Elastic pricing held realized price at $3.45 while rivals promoted deeper, stabilizing snacks share at 16.2% with +2% Q4 organic projected.

In EMEA, 22% of sales, Reckitt's Lysol and Henkel's Persil partnered with Aldi/Lidl, where private label hit 28%. FreshGlow hair care volumes fell 3% in Germany/UK from deeper promos, plus Brexit logistics.

We premiumized with GlowPro salon extensions DTC on Amazon, growing online 35% to 12% regional revenue. Sephora/Boots partnerships added 450 bps ACV, and SAP S/4HANA cut stockouts 40% for PCR bottles, defending 21% share and lifting EMEA margins 110 bps to 48.2%.

In APAC, 18% of sales, China's Yili and Indonesia's Wings grew 15%; India's Britannia took 1.5 points from VitalEats.

We localized with AsiaFit low-sugar green teas, gaining 5% modern trade distribution, 12% volume. $15 million on WeChat/Shopee hit 28% ROAS. Vietnam nearshoring cut lead times 25% amid palm oil volatility.

Forward, with 12% promo depth expected, our $200 million Defend & Grow initiative—40% innovation, 30% trade/A&P, 30% tech—protects 1-2% share, with upside from 15 launches like microbiome skincare.

Next, some color on price elasticity observations, central amid consumer resets. Our blended elasticity was -1.1 this quarter, better than -1.3 in Q2 and -1.4 in 2023 peak inflation, as US CPI cools to 2.5% and Europe to 1.8%. This means a 1% ASP rise led to 1.1% volume drop, offset by mix for 4.2% organic growth, with private labels at 28%.

By category, household care was inelastic at -0.7 like P&G; UltraClean took 2% price, volumes -1.4% with 15% super-premium share. Snacks/beverages more elastic at -1.6 like PepsiCo Frito-Lay; ChipBlitz 4% ASP hike caused -6.4% volume vs. Aldi/Lidl, countered by value packs adding 8% basket size.

North America improved to -1.0, premium to private labels at 22%, e-comm Subscribe & Save up 12% repeats; Gen Z EnergyBoost at -0.9. Europe -1.3, personal care -1.4 vs. Tesco private label 32%, but Southern Europe -1.0 on tourism.

EMs best at -0.8; Brazil/India traded down less, soaps +18% value share via sachets adding 5M households.

AI pricing with SymphonyAI optimizes elasticity, 3.8x trade ROI, A+P to 22%. Premium launches target -0.6; expect FY24 -1.05 normalization for 5-7% organic, 2-3 points pricing.

On organic sales growth guidance: Q3 was 4.2%, sixth straight positive, 2.1% volume/2.1% pricing, Health & Wellness +110 bps share on NutriBoost bars with 25% more plant protein.

Q4: 3-5% organic, vs. last year's 6.1%; 1-2% volume on 1,200 NDPs for Refresh vs. Gatorade/Monster, 2-3% pricing on residual cocoa/palm easing 15% YoY.

North America 4-6% (60% of growth), e-comm 18%; Europe flat-+2% on premium Beauty EcoGlow +3% mix; EMs 8-10%, India/Brazil +5% volume on ValueMax pods +80 bps vs. Persil.

FY2025 raised to 4-6% from 3-5%, +$2.5-3.5B on $28B base, 2-3% volume/mix, 2-3% pricing at 2.5% CPI. Enablers: $150M Project Horizon +4% efficiency; 12 launches like zero-sugar Zest for GLP-1 tailwind +15% trial, PureHarvest snacks; elasticity -2.5; 50% recycled +7% velocity.

Risks: US slowdown -2% non-essentials penetration, EM FX. 45% gross margin from $400M ZBB savings gives flexibility; upper-half confident vs. industry 2-3%.

Capital expenditures for FY2024: $1.25B, +4% YoY; 45% maintenance, 35% growth capacity, 15% digital/automation, 5% R&D. ROIC >15%, payback <3 years for 8-10% sales growth, 200bps margin expansion.

Priorities align with resilience, premiumization/health (25%+ CAGR plant-protein), sustainability vs. EU/California regs.

$450M manufacturing: $150M NA robotics/AI like P&G West Virginia for PureEssence pods/CrunchBar +20% throughput, 15% labor gains; $100M EMEA Rotterdam aseptic for dairy alts +25% energy savings.

$400M capacity EMs: $200M Vietnam beverage plant for RTD teas +5% APAC EBITDA; $120M Mexico snacks on 15% savory CAGR; $80M Ohio pet food.

$200M sustainability/digital: $80M renewables to 40% by 2025, 95% zero-waste pilot -30% disposal; $120M SAP/IBM Watson blockchain for cocoa provenance, 70% millennial priority.

NA 45% capex premium/efficiency vs. private label; EMEA 25% compliance; APAC/LATAM 30% volume/beauty.

70% from $2.8B OCF, rest 3.5% debt. FY25 flat $1.25-1.3B for dividends/buybacks.

With that detailed financial overview, next Lisa Chen will share insights on our marketing and brand initiatives.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, John. Our brand building efforts have contributed significantly to our performance. We're seeing strong engagement across channels, especially with our new GlowUp campaign.

Diving into our promotional strategy and effectiveness—a cornerstone driving volume amid private label and retailer pressures. Q3 promo spend was $285 million, 18.2% of sales, up from 17.8% YoY but flat QoQ. Trade 62% ($177M), consumer 38% ($108M). Targeting ROPS >2.8x, tracking 3.1x YTD vs. peers 2.5x, better than Unilever 2.7x/P&G 2.9x.

Promos lifted sales 12.4% average vs. 9.8% last year. FreshStart Beverages +15.2% on Summer Hydrate BOGO/Kroger app, +8% penetration. PureHome cleaners 9.7%, +1.2 ACV vs. Clorox.

AI PromoOptix (SymphonyAI, 15PB POS + loyalty data) cut waste 22%, elasticity to -2.6 (1% discount =2.6% volume).

NA 48% spend, 13.8% lift, Everyday Value endcaps/digital tags +4.2 share household vs. Walmart+; Instacart/DoorDash 4x ROI.

Europe 25%, 11.2% lift; UK Tesco Clubcard Scan & Save +14% EcoGlow volumes, Germany DM +2% vs. Henkel.

APAC 20%, 14.7%; China Tmall 618 FreshStart +28% GMV 3.8x ROI, India kirana PureHome +16% trial.

LATAM 7%, 10.9%; Brazil Carrefour beverages +1.5 vs. Ambev, Mexico OXXO high-margin.

Q4: PromoOptix zero-party, performance trade (20% tied to lift) for 3.5x ROPS; 10% media to CTV/social AR for Gen Z. Underpins 4-6% organic, 150bps margin.

Following me, Mike Patel will discuss supply chain performance.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. We continue to optimize our supply chain network and implement advanced technologies to improve efficiency and resilience. We've nearshored 40% of North American production to Mexico, cutting lead times 25% and shielding from Red Sea delays inflating freight 20%. Vendor-managed inventory with Sysco freed $300M working capital. AI demand sensing improved forecast accuracy 18%, inventory to 62 days, stockouts -30%. RSPO palm 85% in APAC, Scope 1/2 emissions -22%. Project Horizon robotics/predictives +4% efficiency. Localized sourcing, blockchain traceability mitigate volatility. We're also reducing our carbon footprint through Planet Positive, 95% recycled/renewable packaging ahead of targets, solar/biomass for 40% renewables, zero-waste pilots diverting 95%.

After me, Dr. Elena Vasquez will share updates on our product innovation pipeline.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mike. We are excited about our pipeline of innovative products. Our recent launch, VitaBoost Plant-Powered Protein Bars, has been well-received, driving 18% of top-line growth.

New products contributed 18% growth, up from 14%. VitaBoost, with upcycled pea/15g protein (Perfect Day fermentation), targets $12B segment 12% CAGR; 2.5x velocity, 15% ACV Walmart/Kroger, 42% repeats, 3.2 share points, $45M incremental 8% Snacks.

PureFlow Zero-Sugar Waters with nootropics/algae in EMEA/APAC; $8B market 15% growth, 12% UK/Germany penetration Tesco/Rewe NPS 68, 3x velocity €28M 6% Beverages, 40% less plastic +$2.5M EMV.

EcoShield Cleaners LATAM plant enzymes; $25B market 10% clean-label, 22% Brazil share R$35M 5% growth, 18% ACV.

Pipeline: 28 SKUs, R&D $285M 3.2% sales > peers. Pruned 15% low-velocity.

Q3: NutriGlow Collagen Yogurts NA DSM peptides, 28% trial $60M vs. Chobani; SpiceWave Teas APAC ashwagandha AI flavors 30% DTC.

Mid: CRISPR soy Pairwise 20% less oil Snacks FY26 $150M savings; HPP JBT juices 50% shelf life.

NA 65% pipeline health 22% growth; EMEA 20% Green Deal packaging; APAC 10% pea hub 25% millennials; LATAM 5% affordable 15% margins.

AI Insights Engine 85% success, DTC/club +35% velocity, 100% recyclable +12% loyalty. Vs. private label/GLP-1, 20-22% FY24 growth 300-350bps organic, 18-month TTM agile.

Finally, Tom Hargrove will discuss our sales performance and channel strategy.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Elena. We are focused on expanding distribution and sales execution. E-commerce is 22% of sales, up 15 points, DTC app +45% personalization. China beauty +2.5 share AR try-on. NDPs 1,200 Refresh. Rural India 85% villages +18% volume. Brazil beverages +3.1 share localized QuenchMex. Modern trade APAC +5%, kirana digitization. Quick-commerce Gojek. Retail partnerships Walmart/Albertsons/Tesco/Sephora boosted ACV. Trade execution reclaimed shelf from private labels. Strong growth in e-commerce and retail investments position us well.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions: Press star then 1 on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from Jane Doe with Goldman Sachs.

Jane Doe:
How is your company addressing the increasing demand for sustainable products?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Great question, Jane. Sustainability is core to our innovation and growth. We've achieved 95% recycled or renewable plastic packaging ahead of 2025 targets, partnering with Amcor on rPET. Zero Waste by 2030 cut Scope 1/2 emissions 22% QoQ, SBTi-validated. Europe EcoHarvest/GlowEssence +9% sales from EU Directive resonance. APAC RSPO palm 85%, Planet Positive 50% recycled EM packs by year-end for Gen Z premium. Recyclable PureFlow/EcoShield, 100% new launches recyclable +12% loyalty, +7% eco-goods velocity vs. Colgate. Unlocks green financing $200M at 50bps below market, MSCI AA rating. Microbiome skincare pipeline aligns too.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lee with JPMorgan.

Mike Lee:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Tom Hargrove:
Thanks, Mike. EMs are key, 38% sales growing 8.7%. APAC +11.2%, China +14.5% GlowEssence Tmall/JD +2.2 share, India +10.8% CrunchBar Shakti 85% villages +18% volume. LATAM +7.9%, Brazil +9.2% PowerClean sachets +3.1 beverages share. Africa +6.4% Nigeria recovery. Route-to-market: Gojek quick-comm, Vietnam plant, Mexico nearshoring. Kirana digitization Reliance, modern trade Tesco Lotus. E-comm 15% EM target FY25, localization low-water pods/ValueMax +80bps share. Urban millennials/aspirational portfolio adds 1.5B consumers by 2030.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Morgan Stanley.

Sarah Kim:
Can you discuss the impact of inflation on your pricing strategy and consumer demand?

John Ramirez:
Sure, Sarah. Inflation cooling helps, but we've observed elasticity at -1.1 blended, improved from -1.4 peak. Pricing contributed 2.1-4.2% to organic, inelastic essentials -0.7 (UltraClean 2% price -1.4% volume), elastic snacks -1.6 countered by packs. NA -1.0 resilient, EM -0.8 aspirational sachets +11% volume. AI SymphonyAI optimizes, elasticity modeling 3.8x ROI. Premium tiers -0.6 target, hold list steady more trade on heroes like P&G. FY25 2-3% pricing at 2.5% CPI, elasticity -1.05 normalization, volume offset for 4-6% organic despite private label 28%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Chen with Bank of America.

David Chen:
How are you leveraging artificial intelligence to improve your supply chain efficiency?

Mike Patel:
Excellent point, David. AI is transformative. Palantir-like demand forecasting -15% inventory, 98% availability, +18% accuracy to 62 days. PromoOptix ML elasticity SKU-store-week 22% waste cut. SAP S/4HANA IBM Watson predictive, blockchain cocoa/palm RSPO. MindSphere IoT Siemens ABB robots +20% throughput Kansas City, 15% labor gains. SAP demand sensing -40% stockouts EMEA. Project Horizon predictive analytics +4% efficiency vs. Red Sea 20% freight. Enables precision, VMI $300M WC, nearshoring 25% leads.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions and participation. To tie back to our key strategic priorities and progress under our Growth Through Precision framework—delivering 7% organic this quarter vs. industry 3.5% NielsenIQ—we've executed sharply amid 25% cocoa/15% palm inflation.

Priority 1: Portfolio optimization/premiumization—divested legacy cleaners $150M proceeds to $400M PlantPure acquisition; premium now 42% revenue vs. 35%, 4.2% price/mix +180bps margin, NA snacks +1.8 to 14.2% IRI.

Priority 2: Sustainability/ESG—95% packaging recycled, 22% emissions cut, Europe +9% EcoHarvest, APAC RSPO 85%, AA MSCI, $200M green financing.

Priority 3: Digital/e-comm—AI Palantir forecast +18% accuracy, e-comm 22% +15pts, DTC +45% ML recs, China +2.5 beauty AR.

Priority 4: Geo expansion/resilience—NA +5%, LATAM +3.1 beverages, APAC +12% India sachets 8% penetration, 40% nearshoring -25% leads, VMI $300M.

This compounds to $1.2B EBITDA +11%, reaffirming FY 6-8% organic, 100bps+ expansion. Confident in long-term sustainable growth and shareholder value. Look forward to next quarter.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the GCB Q3 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Geographic performance: developed vs. emerging markets
Organic sales growth guidance for next quarter/year
New product launches and innovation pipeline update

aspect_summary.Geographic performance: developed vs. em: Developed markets (62% revenue) grew 3.2% organically (NA +4.1%, Europe +1.8%), with margins up 80 bps to 28.5% from efficiencies. Emerging markets (38% revenue) grew 8.7% (APAC +11.2%, India +10.8%, LATAM +7.9%, Africa +6.4%), contributing 60% volume growth but margins down 50 bps to 22.1% from raw material costs; EM outgrew developed by 5.5 points.
aspect_summary.Key strategic priorities and progress: Growth Through Precision framework: 1) Portfolio optimization/premiumization (premium 42% revenue, divested low-growth brands); 2) Sustainability/ESG (95% recycled packaging, 22% emissions cut, RSPO palm 85%); 3) Digital/e-comm (22% sales, AI forecasting); 4) Geo expansion/resilience (EM growth, nearshoring, route-to-market innovations like quick-commerce). Delivered 7% organic vs. industry 3.5%.
aspect_summary.Competitive activity and response: NA: P&G Tide Pods (+1.2 pts share), PepsiCo Gatorade (+2.1 pts), Mondelez Oreo; countered with recyclable pouches, trade spend (+$25M), relaunches (VitalBoost). EMEA: Reckitt/Henkel/private labels; premiumized GlowPro, partnerships. APAC: Yili/Wings/Britannia; localized products, digital spend. $200M Defend & Grow initiative (innovation/trade/tech) to protect 1-2% share.
aspect_summary.Organic sales growth guidance for next q: Q4: 3-5% organic (NA 4-6%, Europe flat to +2%, EM 8-10%). FY2025: raised to 4-6% (+$2.5-3.5B on $28B base; 2-3% volume/mix, 2-3% pricing).
aspect_summary.Promotional strategy and effectiveness: Q3 spend $285M (18.2% sales; trade 62%, consumer 38%), ROPS 3.1x (vs. peers 2.5-2.9x), lifted sales 12.4%. AI PromoOptix cut waste 22%, elasticity -2.6. Regional lifts: NA 13.8%, Europe 11.2%, APAC 14.7%. Q4: 3.5x ROPS target, performance-tied trade.
aspect_summary.Capital expenditure plans and priorities: FY2024: $1.25B (+4% YoY; 45% maintenance, 35% growth capacity, 15% digital/automation, 5% R&D; ROIC >15%). Priorities: $450M manufacturing (NA robotics, EMEA aseptic), $400M EM capacity (Vietnam, Mexico), $200M sustainability/digital (renewables, blockchain). FY25: flat $1.25-1.3B.
aspect_summary.Price elasticity observations: Blended -1.1 (improved from -1.3 Q2, -1.4 2023); household -0.7, snacks -1.6. Regional: NA -1.0, Europe -1.3, EM -0.8. AI optimizes (3.8x ROI); FY24 target -1.05 for 5-7% organic.
aspect_summary.New product launches and innovation pipe: New products drove 18% growth: VitaBoost protein bars ($45M, 3.2 pts share), PureFlow zero-sugar waters (€28M), EcoShield cleaners (R$35M).
